subject.title: [Feature]: Support external unified session storage for stateless session mode

question: Should external shared session storage be a core backend contract, a plugin/SDK backend seam, or deferred behind the broader database-abstraction work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the backend owner changes config shape, credentials, migrations, consistency semantics, dependency policy, transcript lifecycle, and plugin compatibility.

options.title: Design session backend contract
options.body: Define a maintainer-approved session/transcript storage contract after aligning with the SQLite flip so external shared backends can be added without a one-off Redis/Mongo path.

options.title: Expose plugin or SDK seam first
options.body: Keep core storage lean and add only the extension hooks needed for owner-maintained external storage plugins to implement shared backends.

options.title: Defer to database abstraction
options.body: Wait for the broader SQLite/Postgres database-abstraction decision and then revisit whether a session-specific external backend remains necessary.

recommendation.title: Design session backend contract
recommendation.body: Define a maintainer-approved session/transcript storage contract after aligning with the SQLite flip so external shared backends can be added without a one-off Redis/Mongo path.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the active session/transcript storage migration lane that this external-backend design must coordinate with.
